title: Staged customer preview streams with consistent snapshotting and manifest pointer
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Context:
We currently produce scheduled CSV exports and webhooks for customer usage. Console product teams want a low-latency "preview" experience inside the Console so customers can see near-real-time usage updates without waiting for full scheduled exports. The preview must be inexpensive, safe (no PII leakage), and operationally simple to debug.

Goal:
- Implement a streaming 'preview' export pipeline that emits per-tenant deltas to short-lived S3 objects + a small atomic manifest pointer.
- Provide a contract that Console can poll to show a live preview feed with < 90s 99th percentile latency for common workloads.
- Guarantee consistent snapshot semantics for reads during retries: each manifest points to a monotonic sequence id and snapshot token so clients can reconcile ordering.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing full scheduled archival exports (CSV, large parquet workloads) in this ticket.
- Not implementing multi-tenant fused manifests — each tenant gets isolated manifests and objects.

Design overview:
1) Producer: exporter-service ingests usage events from the analytics pipeline (Kafka). Events are bucketed into sliding windows (configurable, default 60s) per tenant. For each window we produce a delta object (newline-delimited minimal JSON rows) and write to a tenant-scoped S3 path: s3://redwood-exports/previews/{tenant_id}/seq={seq}/delta.ndjson. Objects are uploaded with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and signed URLs are short-lived (5m) for Console.

2) Atomic manifest: once a delta object is successfully uploaded and checksum-verified, exporter-service writes/updates a small manifest JSON to s3://redwood-exports/previews/{tenant_id}/manifest.json which contains: {"seq": "<monotonic_seq>", "snapshot_token": "<opaque_hash>", "delta_key": "<s3_key>", "size_bytes": "<n>", "started_at": "<ISO>"}. The manifest update uses an atomic S3 overwrite; Console treats manifest writes as the single source of truth.

3) Idempotency & retries: exporter-service generates opaque delivery tokens for each manifest update. If upload retries occur, manifest sequence numbers are strictly increasing and snapshot_token is computed from the sorted set of event checksums for the seq to enable dedupe on the client side.

4) Fallback: if S3 upload or manifest update fails repeatedly, exporter-service falls back to triggering the scheduled batch export path and annotates the tenant manifest with an "incomplete" flag so Console can surface degraded preview.

5) Access patterns: Console will poll the manifest endpoint with If-None-Match using snapshot_token to avoid unnecessary downloads. Signed URL fetching is done by Console frontend via short-lived GET to S3 with HTTPS.

Operational guarantees / SLOs:
- Preview manifest visibility latency: 90s p99 from event ingestion -> manifest update.
- Event loss tolerance: zero-loss within sliding window (best-effort). Any events that fail persistently are reported to an "export-failures" counter and tied to on-call alerts.
- Cost: aim for < 10% incremental S3 PUT volume relative to daily scheduled exports by batch compressing small deltas and TTL (keep deltas 1 hour).

Schema and contract for manifest.json (consumer-facing):
- seq: string (monotonic integer as string)
- snapshot_token: string (opaque hex, used for ETag/If-None-Match)
- delta_key: string (full S3 key to get ndjson)
- size_bytes: string
- started_at: string (ISO8601)
- status: string (ready | incomplete | degraded)
- signature_v: string (optional, if we sign manifests for additional integrity checks)

Security & compliance:
- All objects SSE-KMS; manifests are NOT public. Console obtains short-lived presigned GETs from control-plane auth service which checks tenant ACLs and device session.
- No raw customer prompt text is surfaced in preview. Preview rows use aggregated buckets and hashed identifiers. Data classification doc: confluence.link/preview-data-classification.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- exporter.preview.latency_ms p50/p90/p99 per-tenant
- exporter.preview.upload_failures counter with tag {tenant_id}
- manifest.stale.gauge (seconds since last manifest update)
- Grafana dashboard and alert: manifest.stale > 600s for top-10 tenants -> PagerDuty P1.

Runbook (high-level):
- If alert fires: check exporter logs, S3 error codes, and Kafka consumer lag.
- Quick fix: restart exporter-service worker for affected tenant pool.
- Workaround for customers: flip preview to "disabled" in Console until resolved (feature flag).

Rollout plan:
1) Internal canary: enable for 3 internal tenants (redwood-staging-*) for 1 week.
2) Beta group: opt-in for 50 small tenants (low throughput) for 2 weeks, monitor latency and costs.
3) Gradual ramp: 10% of eligible tenants / day with automated safety gates (manifest latency, upload error rate).
4) Full GA when safety gates stable for 7 days.

Acceptance criteria:
- exporter-service writes manifests with correct monotonic seq and snapshot_token for test tenants under load test.
- Console can poll and render preview using manifest and delta objects without duplication or reordering for 99% of windows in load test.
- Observability dashboard shows exporter.preview.latency and alerts configured.
- Security review sign-off recorded in Confluence and KMS key policy updated.

Deliverables / tasks (high level):
- implement producer batching and delta writer (service changes)
- manifest writer with seq generation and token hash function
- auth endpoint for presigned GETs with tenant ACL checks
- Console polling integration and dedupe logic using snapshot_token
- dashboards, alerts, runbook, and security review

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Preview+Streams+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1426 (WIP)
- Load test script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/loadtests/preview-streams
acceptance_criteria: Manifest semantics documented and implemented for canonical tenants
Console renders previews correctly under 50x baseline traffic in staging
Monitoring & alerts deployed to Grafana and Oncall configured
Security review completed and KMS policy applied
comments: 2025-02-11 - Maya Chen: Initial spike showed S3 PUT cost higher than expected for 60s windows. We prototyped compressing ndjson using gzip and observed 6x reduction for small deltas.
2025-02-13 - Jon Park (PM): Please ensure we expose a 'preview health' metric to customers (Console banner) when status != ready.

2025-02-16 - Engineering review: agreed to use monotonic seq generator backed by ZK ephemeral node per-tenant to avoid clock skew. Risks: ZK availability. Alternative: DynamoDB conditional increment (fallthrough).
2025-02-18 - Security review note: KMS key alias redwood/preview-exports created; RBAC audit required before beta.
2025-02-22 - PR 1426 updated: added snapshot_token calculation and unit tests for dedupe algorithm. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/1426
2025-02-25 - Maya Chen: Started staging canary for 3 tenants under redwood-staging. Observed p99 latency 78s; upload_failures 0.2% during spike. Moving to beta if next 48h stable.
